Q: What are the common Wi-Fi frequency bands?
Option2: 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz

Q: What is a key characteristic of the 2.4 GHz band?
Option1: Many non-overlapping channels with low interference
Option2: Longer range and better wall penetration but fewer non-overlapping channels

Q: What is a key characteristic of the 5 GHz band?
Option2: Shorter range but many non-overlapping channels and typically less interference

Q: What is the main purpose of channel planning?
Option2: Reduce co-channel/adjacent-channel interference by placing access points on non-overlapping channels

Q: Which statement about regulations is true in Wi-Fi channel selection?
Option2: Regulatory domains define allowed channels and transmit power; devices must obey local rules
Option3: Users can freely transmit at any power

Q: Which statement compares 2.4 GHz vs 5 GHz channels?
Option2: 5 GHz typically offers many more non-overlapping channels than 2.4 GHz, allowing denser deployments

Q: What is Bluetooth used for?
Option2: Short-range personal area networking for accessories like headsets and keyboards

What is long-range fixed wireless (licensed) typically used for?
Option2: Point-to-point/point-to-multipoint links using licensed spectrum for interference management and service-provider backhaul

Q: What is long-range fixed wireless (unlicensed)?
Option2: Outdoor links using unlicensed bands (for example, 5 GHz, 60 GHz) subject to local power/antenna regulations

Q: What do power limits in regulations accomplish for wireless?
Option2: Control maximum transmit strength and antenna gain to minimize interference and ensure safety

Q: What is Near-field communication (NFC)?
Option2: Very short-range (a few centimeters) contactless communication used for pairing and payments
Option3: A fixed wireless standard for miles

Q: What is Radio-frequency identification (RFID)?
Option2: Tag/reader system where small tags are powered (passive) or self-powered (active) and identified by radio

Q: Which wireless band is typically preferred for dense apartment deployments to avoid interference?
Option2: 5 GHz with careful channel planning

Q: A device needs long range and wall penetration rather than peak throughput. Which band is usually better?
Option2: 2.4 GHz

Q: An office experiences poor Wi-Fi due to overlapping channels on every access point. Best first fix?
Option1: Increase transmit power on all access points
Option2: Reassign access points to non-overlapping channels and adjust power
